active_ingredients.name: Chromobacterium subtsugae strain PRAA4-1T cells and spent fermentation media

rates.interval: Turf foliar application for labeled surface-feeding insects; do not irrigate after application
Turf application for white grubs and annual bluegrass weevil; use at least 100 gal water/acre and irrigate after application to moisten the top inch of soil
Turf soil treatment for low-to-medium populations of labeled nematodes
Turf soil drench or injection in 100-150 gal water/acre
Hand-held or backpack sprayer; approximates 0.5-3 lb product/100 gal water

products.notes: For organic production; OMRI listed on the specimen label. Potency is at least 1,000 Cabbage Looper Killing Units (CLKU) per mg. For conventional ground sprays, use at least 10 gal total volume/acre. Maintain agitation and do not let spray mixture stand overnight. Product is most effective against new populations and recently hatched immature pests and is not systemic. For armyworms, cutworms, webworms, chinch bugs, or leafhoppers, do not irrigate after application. For white grubs and annual bluegrass weevil, use at least 100 gal water/acre, irrigate afterward to moisten the top inch of soil, and apply shortly after egg hatch at first or second instar; no more than 0.5 inch of thatch should be present. For nematodes, watered-in placement in the soil profile is required. Soil drench insect treatments may be repeated at 10- to 14-day intervals. Keep solution pH from 6 to 8, with neutral preferred. Toxic to aquatic invertebrates, certain non-target terrestrial arthropods, and bees; do not apply while bees are visiting the treatment area. Keep unprotected persons out of non-agricultural treated areas until sprays have dried. Follow the current label.
